+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8280'
+title: Give a tool a run-to-completion mode, and validate waitSeconds against timeout
+---
+A host cannot say "this tool blocks until it is done and never parks". A host that tries to say it with the clocks we give gets behaviour we do not intend.
+
+## The host requirement
+
+The `FoundationModelsMultitool` session has a discovery tool. A model cannot write a snippet until it knows which paths exist, so discovery is a synchronous prerequisite. If discovery parks, the model gets a pending envelope for a call it must go and collect. They measured that result and it was bad: every discovery call parked, the model never got the catalogue, and three runs ended with no tool calls and an answer that said it had no access.
+
+So they need the tool to block. They ask for it with `waitSeconds = timeout = 86_400`.
+
+## What those values do
+
+`waitSeconds >= timeout` is not implemented as "never detach". Nothing implements that reading.
+
+- Both clocks clamp through `SessionMailbox.boundedNanoseconds(clamping:)` with the same `ToolContext.waitSecondsCeiling` (`Hosting/DetachingTool.swift:420-427` and `:580-587`). The name is wrong at the second site.
+- `DetachConfiguration.init` (`:100-108`) and the per-call override (`:358-360`) store both clocks with no validation and no relational check.
+- The two clocks are independent timers started at the same time. They never consult each other.
+
+So with 86400 and 86400 the call blocks in band for a full day, and then the clocks race. `waitSeconds` arms with fewer scheduling hops, so it usually wins: the call detaches, and the timeout watcher then stops the run it just parked (`:565-570`). The model gets a pending token for a dead run. If the race goes the other way, `call` throws `DetachingToolError.timedOut` in band. Which one you get is timing.
+
+Our stock design assumes the opposite relation. `DetachingTool.swift:61-65` says the 120 second timeout is "deliberately much longer than" the 5 second wait "so at stock settings the soft deadline always wins". The host inverted that, and no code defends the inversion.
+
+## Missing tests
+
+`Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/SessionMailboxTests.swift:66-83` covers only the low end of the clamp: `-1.0`, `0.0`, `NaN`. No test refers to `waitSecondsCeiling`. No test uses `waitSeconds == timeout` or `waitSeconds > timeout`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] A host can ask for run-to-completion directly, and the request is clear in the API
+- [ ] In that mode the tool never parks, and only a real error reaches the model
+- [ ] `waitSeconds >= timeout` is rejected, or it is given a defined and documented behaviour
+- [ ] The race between the two clocks cannot give the model a token for a run that is already dead
+- [ ] Tests cover `waitSeconds == timeout`, `waitSeconds > timeout`, and the ceiling
+- [ ] The misleading use of `waitSecondsCeiling` as the timeout ceiling is corrected or renamed
+
+Reported by the `FoundationModelsMultitool` session (their card `^bffrdpr`). #api #nested-generation
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    ### Research — what the code shows, and the design chosen
+
+    Read `Hosting/DetachingTool.swift` whole, `Hosting/ToolContext.swift` and `Hosting/SessionMailbox.swift` around the clamp, and every `DetachConfiguration` construction site.
+
+    Facts:
+
+    - `Mode.runToCompletion` already exists, but it is "bounded only by `timeout`", so it cannot be the mode the consumer needs: a timeout that fires reports a slow search as a failed search. Nothing in the package can say "no clock at all".
+    - No source file builds `DetachConfiguration(mode: .runToCompletion, ...)`. Only `nativeSessionMount` is used inside the package (`Session/ToolOutputCapping.swift`). Every `.runToCompletion` construction is in tests or in the sibling packages.
+    - The race: `raceSettlement` returns `.deadlineElapsed`, then `detach()` calls `funnel.markDetached(...)`, which refuses only when the run has already **settled**. The timeout watcher decides to kill the run some time BEFORE `settleRun` lands, so a detach that arrives in that window parks a run the timeout is killing.
+    - Existing test intervals stay valid under a `waitSeconds < timeout` rule: `generousInterval` is 30 and the stock timeout is 120.
+
+    Design chosen:
+
+    1. `timeout` becomes `TimeInterval?`. `nil` means "no clock at all". New `DetachConfiguration.runToCompletionMount` = `.runToCompletion` with `timeout: nil` — the one name a host asks for run-to-completion by. It is NOT a long timeout; the timeout watcher is never started.
+    2. The clock relation is rejected, not clamped. `DetachingTool.call` resolves the effective clocks (wrap-time configuration merged with the per-call `DetachmentParameterProviding` override) and throws `DetachingToolError.invalidClocks` before any work starts when the mode is `.detaching` and `waitSeconds >= timeout`. One predicate, one enforcement point, so the wrap-time site and the per-call site cannot disagree. The error text names `runToCompletionMount` as the migration.
+       A `precondition` in `DetachConfiguration.init` was rejected: a library must not kill its host over a configuration value, the per-call site takes model-supplied numbers and can never trap, and a trap cannot be tested.
+    3. `RunEventFunnel` gains `beginTimeout()`. The timeout watcher claims the run before it resolves the race, and `markDetached` refuses a claimed run, so `detach()` returns the in-band timeout instead of a token for a run that is already dead.
+    4. `ToolContext.waitSecondsCeiling` is renamed `deadlineSecondsCeiling` — it bounds every seconds-valued deadline the run plane clamps (the `wait` deadline, `waitSeconds`, and `timeout`), so the name is correct at each of the three sites.

+  text: |-
+    ### What landed, and the public API it changes
+
+    Four changes, all in `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter`.
+
+    **1. The run-to-completion mount.** `DetachConfiguration.timeout` is now `TimeInterval?`, where `nil` means no clock at all, and `DetachConfiguration.runToCompletionMount` is the pair a host asks for the mode by: `.runToCompletion` with `timeout: nil`. `raceInnerAgainstTimeout` starts no watcher for a `nil` timeout, so nothing but the wrapped tool's own failure can reach the model. This is not a long timeout, and the mount's own doc says why a long timeout is not a substitute.
+
+    **2. The clock relation is rejected.** `DetachConfiguration.clockRelationFailure(tool:mode:waitSeconds:timeout:)` is the one implementation of the rule: in `.detaching`, with a stated timeout, `waitSeconds` must stand strictly under `timeout`. `DetachingTool.call` applies it to the clocks the call actually resolved to — the wrap-time configuration merged with a `DetachmentParameterProviding` override — and throws `DetachingToolError.invalidClocks` before any work starts, so a refused call leaves no run, no parked token and no event. Checking at that one point covers both sites the card names.
+
+    **3. The migration is in the rejection.** `DetachingToolError` now conforms to `CustomStringConvertible`, so the sentence a model and a host read for `invalidClocks` names the tool, both clocks, and `DetachConfiguration.runToCompletionMount` as the thing to move to. A consumer on 86400/86400 gets that sentence on the first call instead of a day-long block and a race.
+
+    **4. The race is closed at the funnel.** `RunEventFunnel.beginTimeout()` claims the run the moment a whole timeout window is known to have elapsed, before the timeout resolves its race, and `markDetached(postingIfSilent:)` refuses a claimed run. A soft deadline elapsing in the same instant now takes the in-band timeout rather than parking a run the watcher is killing. `RunEventFunnel` moved from file-private to internal so that one decision can be tested directly.
+
+    **Renamed:** `ToolContext.waitSecondsCeiling` is now `ToolContext.deadlineSecondsCeiling`. One ceiling bounds every seconds-valued deadline the run plane clamps — the `wait` deadline, `waitSeconds`, and `timeout` — so the name is correct at each of the three sites.
+
+    **Public API changes, for consumers:**
+
+    - `DetachConfiguration.timeout` and the `timeout:` parameter of its initializer are now `TimeInterval?`. Passing a number still compiles unchanged; reading the property now reads an optional.
+    - `ToolContext.waitSecondsCeiling` is renamed `ToolContext.deadlineSecondsCeiling`. No alias is kept.
+    - `DetachingToolError` gains `invalidClocks(tool:waitSeconds:timeout:)` and a `description`. The `timedOut` case now renders as a sentence rather than as its own reflection, which changes the text of a timed-out run's terminal `detail`.
+    - New: `DetachConfiguration.runToCompletionMount`.
+
+    **How the tests were driven.** Each new test named a symbol that did not exist — `runToCompletionMount`, `invalidClocks`, `beginTimeout`, `deadlineSecondsCeiling` — so the suite would not build until the implementation landed. That build failure is the red state each test started from; no test was written after the code it exercises.

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m05wjg931dbwd53aykk7tszx
+  text: |-
+    ### The mode is now declared for each tool — shape 1, and why
+
+    The consumer is right, and the gap is closed with shape 1: **a tool declares its mount the way it declares its clocks.**
+
+    `DetachmentParameterProviding` gains one requirement, with a default:
+
+    ```swift
+    var detachmentMount: DetachConfiguration? { get }   // default: nil
+    ```
+
+    `DetachingTool.init` resolves it once: `(wrapped as? any DetachmentParameterProviding)?.detachmentMount ?? configuration`. A tool that declares nothing keeps the configuration its composition site passed, so nothing that works today changes.
+
+    **Why the whole mount, and not only `mode`.** The card offered `mode`, but a mode alone cannot say what the consumer needs. In `.runToCompletion` the wrap-time `timeout` still bounds the work, and a `nil` clock in `detachmentClocks(from:)` means "fall back", never "no clock". So a tool that declared only its mode while mounted on `.nativeSessionMount` would still carry the 120 second timeout — a slow search reported as a failed search, which is the thing they refuse. `DetachConfiguration.runToCompletionMount` states mode and no-clock together, and that is exactly the name a tool now writes.
+
+    **Why shape 1 and not shape 2 (a configuration for each tool at the mount site).** The mount site takes `[any Tool]` from `RoutedModel.makeSession(tools:)`. To choose per tool there, the host would have to carry a parallel map through `makeSession`, `makeSessionToolWiring`, `fork`, and `restoreSessionTree` — a much wider public break — and it would put the policy in the host, far from the tool that knows. The declaration also reaches every composition site at once, `ToolInvoker`'s inner `tools.*` mount included, with no plumbing. Their own `SearchToolsTool.swift` already says the tool is what needs to state this.
+
+    **Precedence.** The tool's declaration wins over the site's configuration, clock and all: a tool declares a mount only for behaviour it cannot work without, so a site that overrode it would hand the tool behaviour its author refused. `detachmentClocks(from:)` still narrows a declared mount further, being the statement about one call rather than about every call.
+
+    **Also defaulted:** `detachmentClocks(from:)` now has a blanket default of `(nil, nil)`. So a tool that only needs the mount writes only `detachmentMount`, and the consumer can delete the 86400/86400 clocks method outright.
+
+    ### Answer: `DetachConfiguration.defaultTimeoutSeconds` is NOT optional
+
+    It stays `public static let defaultTimeoutSeconds: TimeInterval = 120`. There is no fourth source break. Only two things became optional: the stored property `DetachConfiguration.timeout` and the `timeout:` parameter of its initializer. Reading the static into a `TimeInterval` still compiles, and the test `stockTimeoutStaysNonOptional` binds it into a plain `TimeInterval` so a later change to that type breaks the build.
+
+    ### The test that proves the real shape
+
+    `oneSessionMountsBothModes` mounts two tools through the ONE `ToolDetachment.sessionMounted` site, under one session identity, one mailbox and one outbox: `DeclaredRunToCompletionTool`, which declares `.runToCompletionMount`, and `ZeroWaitDetachingTool`, which declares no mount. The detaching one parks and returns a pending envelope; the declaring one blocks past the stock soft deadline the session mount carries, and exactly one run is parked — the detaching tool's.
+
+    **That test earned its red.** The first version held the blocking call for only 0.6 seconds and PASSED against an engine that ignored the declaration, because the session mount's own `waitSeconds` is 5 and neither tool had parked yet. Measured, and then fixed: the hold now runs past `DetachConfiguration.defaultWaitSeconds`. With the resolution removed the test reports `parked.count → 2` and hands the catalogue call a pending envelope — the consumer's exact failure. Do not shorten that hold; a fast version of this test proves nothing.
